findings.summary: Public source registration can follow an in-case symlink and overwrite another case artifact because it bypasses the whole-case scan.
findings.exploit: A shared case can contain data/raw/new-id/payload.csv as a symlink to case.json. register_local_source resolves the root and calls resume_case, but neither scans the whole tree; validate_case_documents ignores an unregistered raw entry. _under_root accepts the destination because the symlink resolves inside the case, and the new-source branch calls dest.write_bytes, which follows the link and replaces case.json with CSV bytes. The installed run_workflow path is protected, but this public resume/write path is not.
findings.remediation: Run the no-symlink/special-file scan at every public case boundary, preferably in the common resume guard before any read or write, and make owned-path helpers reject every symlink component even when its target remains under the root. Add a direct register_local_source regression using an in-root symlink target and assert zero mutation.

findings.summary: Resume trusts a completed-state map when required artifact identities are absent, allowing a shared case to claim P7 completion without validation.
findings.exploit: changed_identities iterates only entries already present in state['identities']. load_snapshot passes a missing or non-mapping identity set as {}, so no change is reported. A portable shared case can therefore set sequential completed entries through P7, status complete, and omit identities; load_snapshot projects README completion and resolve_workflow returns complete without hashing any source, prepared data, Gate A, detector, draft, replay, review, or Gate B artifact.
findings.remediation: Validate the durable-state schema and derive the required identity names from the last completed phase. Missing, malformed, or extra authoritative identity state must fail closed or invalidate from the earliest affected phase; recompute and compare every required artifact identity before honoring completion.

findings.summary: Canonical-equivalent Unicode identities bypass Gate A/reviewer/Gate B role separation.
findings.exploit: The separation checks compare identity.casefold() values, while _required_identity only strips whitespace. Unicode canonical equivalents remain unequal without normalization—for example Gate A approver 'Café' and reviewer 'Cafe\u0301'. The same person can therefore satisfy both roles; the identical weakness exists between reviewer and Gate B journalist at line 140.
findings.remediation: Validate identities through one shared canonical identity function that rejects controls and normalizes NFC before case folding. Compare only canonical identities at Gate A, P6 attestation/reviewer binding, and Gate B, while preserving the display form separately. Add composed/decomposed and case-variant separation tests for both gates.

findings.summary: Attempt failure persistence redacts only three token prefixes and leaks common credentials from dynamic-owner exceptions.
findings.exploit: safe_error reaches _safe_text, whose only secret patterns are sk_live_, ghp_, and github_pat_. run_attempts writes that text to failure.json, events.jsonl, state.failures, and blocked_reason. A P5/P6 runtime exception containing 'Authorization: Bearer ...', 'token=super-secret-token', 'password=...', an AWS key, or a credential-bearing URL is persisted verbatim across up to three attempts. review.py already demonstrates the broader assignment/Bearer/token-prefix redaction needed at this boundary.
findings.remediation: Centralize the broad credential sanitizer and apply it to error text, event fields, blocked reasons, and persisted attempt results before truncation. Cover assignment forms, Bearer values, common provider prefixes, and credential-bearing URLs without rewriting structural identifiers; add a dynamic-owner failure regression that inspects every durable surface.
